The recovery runner differs solely in import/root resolution, document null guard, restored cases, skipping already completed cases and provenance checks outside the timed loop.

rasterComparison.interpretation: Same common-post profile and measured harness before/after removing unused normal/specular/velocity attachments. Every channel is decoded; only the observed before repeat range is accepted. Performance remains a sequential local comparison, not a cross-engine quality claim.

contention.interpretation: Both counters refer to the same adapter. External compute contention was observed during recovery; speed comparisons involving these cases are not isolated. Earlier runs were not audited for external GPU isolation.

provenance: Baseline source and dist were built together before edits; its compiled dist stayed unchanged until its 36 cases and wet views completed. Native/common after-runs execute identical rebuilt source, dist and measured harness. Before/after harness fingerprints differ because profile selection and post-measurement auditing were added; original GPU journal, fixture and measured RAF/timing loop remain in use. Default before/after timings are descriptive, not an isolated same-harness performance claim. Common report recovered 24 validated cases and executed 12 remaining cases after a navigation document-readiness error. The failed original report is retained; both original/recovery runner hashes and the exact provenance are included. Recovery changed document null checking and case restoration outside the measured loop. This is a recovered execution, not a successful original run.
interpretation: common-post matches absence of TAA, AO, diffuse bounce, SSR, DOF, bloom and planar reflections. Native PBR, procedural materials, shadow filtering, atmosphere, point-light attenuation, IBL and tone mapping still differ. Equal pixel quality and competitive advantage are not established. Wet views in BOTH after reports exercise the full default engine, independently of the benchmark profile. Strict canonical comparison uses every decoded channel and only the observed baseline repeat range; no tolerance is introduced.
